chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said:

A man asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) while I was listening: Is it permissible to sell fresh juice (unfermented grape juice) from the Magians, Jews, Christians, and Muslims before it ferments, and to take the payment or defer it? He said: 'There is no harm if you sell it as halal, for they know better.' Meaning the juice, and they defer the payment.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadhal said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about al-fuqqa' (a type of fermented drink), and he said: 'It is wine, and in it is the penalty of the drinker of wine.'

key_terms.الْعَصِير: Fresh juice (specifically grape juice) before fermentation
key_terms.الْفُقَّاع: A specific type of fermented drink, often considered wine

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling fresh grape juice before it ferments, and what is the status of fuqqa'?
ai.summary: These narrations from Imam al-Rida (AS) establish the critical distinction between fresh juice (asir) and wine based on the process of fermentation, allowing the sale of unfermented juice to People of the Book and Muslims as it is not yet khamr. The second narration explicitly classifies 'fuqqa'' (a type of fermented drink) as wine, thereby subjecting it to the specific legal penalty (hadd) prescribed for intoxicants. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the prohibition of wine is tied to its intoxicating nature and transformation, rather than its source alone.
